steps.action: RNA (ribonucleic acid) and DNA (deoxyribonucleic acid) are both nucleic acids, but they have several key differences. Structurally, DNA contains the sugar deoxyribose, while RNA contains the sugar ribose, which has one more hydroxyl group. DNA is typically double-stranded, forming a helical shape, whereas RNA is usually single-stranded. The nitrogenous bases in DNA are adenine, thymine, cytosine, and guanine, but in RNA, thymine is replaced by uracil. Functionally, DNA stores genetic information, while RNA plays roles in protein synthesis and regulation as messenger RNA (mRNA), transfer RNA (tRNA), and ribosomal RNA (rRNA). RNA is also involved in various other cellular processes.
